scope: Final raw/optimized native capture and GUI; independent controller counts and exact pixels during physical SDFS, earliest-motion and keyboard visible timing including wrap, native/emulation FASTEST125, cancellation/recovery, loss/counter/epoch boundaries, C preemption, production-link checks and observation-disabled replay.

controller_quantization: 16 scanlines = approximately 1028.505 us, the fastest interval the pinned existing controller can emit while respecting minimum 1 ms spacing. Continuous diagonal input exercises that limit. No source at exactly 1000 Hz was synthesized; the measured worst sample gap is independently required to remain strictly below 1 ms. Faster host bursts are separate negative controls.

memory.note: Cursor mask parity uses two upper bytes; diagnostic source selector uses two additional upper bytes. All code/data fit existing bank reservations. Stack peaks are recorded per run.

fixes: Preserve route-slot indexing with an explicit M=16 annotation after the zero-route exit.
Never delegate a reasserted owned pointer timer edge to the ROM IRQ path while SIO is closed.
Fast idle sample still reads both electrical levels but skips decode/queue work.
Validate physical record timestamp flags and full source identity before GUI translation.
Prepack/cache arrow masks and skip restoration only for conservative disjoint text/bar bounds, including saved edge nibbles.
Repaint only the edited text tile and live glyphs plus the trailing erased glyph. Keep the twelve-tick limit unchanged.
Pixel observer waits for a stable completed frame when disk progress races scanout.
recovery_scope: 128-byte functional queued/active/terminal cancellation, checksum and NAK; traced 128-byte timeout/wrap; one traced 256-byte FASTEST125 active cancellation keeps the payload window open under capture. A traced 128-byte cancellation attempt legitimately completed before cancellation became effective; it is not used as active-cancellation timing evidence.
